before: A reproducible build specifies source files, headers, compiler version, language mode and flags. The command below lists both implementation files; an IDE having remembered an old object file is not a reliable build specification.
Expected output or behavior: 8. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Write an explicit two-stage command sequence and explain which objects a changed header invalidates. You may trace it without a C compiler; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
after: A repeatable build has a clear list of source files, headers, compiler version, language mode, and flags. Do not depend on an editor quietly reusing an old compiled file.
An object file holds a compiled part before final linking. With GCC, `-c` compiles without linking. Build main.c and score.c into main.o and score.o, then link both to supply the complete program.

First run `gcc -std=c17 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -c main.c score.c`. Then run `gcc main.o score.o -o app`. The resulting program prints 8. Leaving score.o out of that final link leaves score's definition missing.
If score.h changes, recompile each source file that includes it before linking again. A build that reuses only unchanged parts is called an incremental build. It still needs to track header changes.

before.question: What happens if the final link omits the score implementation?
choices: The main object already contains every imported function body.
Linking fails with an unresolved score reference.
Header changes never affect a compiled object.
before.explanation: Separate compilation creates object files; linking must still combine all required definitions.

after.question: Leave score.o out of the final link. What happens?
choices: main.o already contains every called function's body.
Linking fails because score's definition is missing.
The header changes can never matter.
after.explanation: Compiling main.c does not copy score's body into it. Linking must include score.o to provide that definition.
